title: Bad-locus contradiction for affine limit fibre dimensions
statement: With the same directed finite-type affine system and surjective comparison maps as in lem-weil-pbc-affine-limit-fibre-dimension-bound, if every stage has a prime whose fibre dimension is strictly greater than d, then the limiting fibre has dimension strictly greater than d; equivalently, the stagewise bad-prime hypothesis contradicts the bound on every limiting fibre.

source.place: Tag 05M5, affine specialization, bad-locus construction and Noetherian fibre stabilization

proof.text: Form the open loci where local fibre dimension is at most d using the bounded-open-upstairs theorem, and take their reduced closed complements. Surjective comparison maps carry bad loci backwards. The affine spectrum limit and nonempty-limit theorem give a compatible limiting bad point. After passage to its residue field, the surjective finite-type fibre system stabilizes by Noetherianity; field-extension invariance of local dimension then contradicts the assumed bound on the limiting fibre.
